How to use Clothing Studio

Make a Roblox outfit in 5 easy steps. You can open this guide again any time with the How to use button at the top.More button, then How to use.

Already have a template? You don't have to start from scratch. Bring in a finished 585×559 picture and see it on the 3D character straight away.

1Pick Shirt or Pants. Use the Shirt / Pants buttons at the top to choose what you're making.
2Choose a color. In the options panel next to the tools, click the color square at the top, or click any of the little colored squares under it.Tap the color square in the bar just above the tools, or tap any of the little colored squares next to it.
3Pick a tool and draw. On the left, chooseIn the tool bar along the bottom, tap Brush to draw, Fill to color a whole area, Text to add words, or Image to add a picture. Swipe that bar sideways for more tools, and tap the tool you're already using to show or hide everything it can do. Then draw on the white grid in the middle.
4The colored boxes are the parts of the clothing (front, back, arms and legs). Color inside the boxes. Your outfit shows up on the character on the right (drag it to spin). Want the character bigger? Drag the line between your drawing and the preview. Or turn on Paint on model in the box below the character and draw straight onto it!Your outfit shows up live in the mini preview in the corner: tap it (or the 3D Preview tab) to see the character full-screen and drag to spin. Turn on Paint on model there to draw straight onto it!
5Export it. When you're happy, click Export Template at the top righttap Export at the top, then upload that picture to Roblox.

Oops: made a mistake?

History: the list on the right of your drawing shows everything you've done; click any step (or press Ctrl+Z) to go backopen More then History to see everything you've done, then tap any step to go back
Clear: wipe the selected layer clean

What the tools do

Brush: draw freehand
Image: upload pictures/logos to your saved library, then click one to place it (they're kept for next time)
Eraser: rub things out
Fill: color a whole area
Pan: slide the whole canvas
Line: draw a straight line
Shape: drag out a box, rounded box, circle or triangle (hold Shift to keep it even, Alt to grow it from the middle). Choose filled, outline only, or both
Text: type words (Enter = new line, bold/italic/underline, align)
Gradient: blend two colors
Picker: copy a color on screen
Stamps: stamp stars, hearts…
Pattern: fill with stripes, dots…
Move: slide something you made
Select: box an area to move or copy. While it's active it also acts as a stencil: everything you paint stays inside it. Shift-drag adds another box, Alt-drag takes one away, and Ctrl+D clears it
Wand: click a colour to select that whole area at once, then copy, move or delete it. Shift-click adds another area, Alt-click takes one away. Tolerance decides how fussy it is about matching
Replace: swap one color for another everywhere (one layer or all)
Smudge: push colors around
Blur: soften an area

More handy buttons

Color picker: full HSV picker with color harmonies
Pixel: hard pixels, no blur (1px brush = 1 pixel)
Symmetry: paint one side and the other side mirrors it live (brush, line, fill, stamps, patterns)
Mirror: flip a layer to the other side of the body. It asks first whether to keep this side too (it puts the mirrored copy on a new layer) or just move the artwork across.
Layer opacity / blend: fade or blend each layer
Duplicate, merge down and flatten buttons in the Layers header (drag a layer row to reorder the stack)
Autosave: your work is saved in this browser as you go; if the tab closes, you'll be offered it back

Keyboard shortcuts

If you know Photoshop, these are the same keys.

B E L G T S I R M V H D P K J U A W: every tool has a letter (hover a tool to see it)
[ and ]: smaller / bigger brush  ·  Shift+[ / ]: softer / harder edge
1…9, 0: set the paint opacity (10%…90%, 100%) while a painting tool is out
Alt + click: grab a colour off the canvas while painting
X swaps Colour 1 and Colour 2
Shift while drawing: straight strokes (Line snaps to 45°)
Shift + click: join a straight line from where your last stroke ended
Stylus pressure: a pen tablet varies the brush width automatically

Selecting

Anything you select is a stencil. While a selection is active, every tool (brush, fill, eraser, blur, even Replace) only works inside it. Press Ctrl+D when you want the whole canvas back.
Ctrl+A: select everything  ·  Ctrl+D: deselect  ·  Ctrl+Shift+I: invert (select the opposite)
Shift + drag: add another area to the selection  ·  Alt + drag: take an area away
Shift + drag (with nothing selected yet): keep the box square
Ctrl+C / X / V: copy, cut & paste  ·  Delete: rub out what's selected
Alt+Backspace: flood the selection with Colour 1  ·  Ctrl+Backspace: with Colour 2

Layers, undo & the canvas

Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: undo / redo anything (Ctrl+Shift+Z also redoes)
Ctrl+J: duplicate the layer  ·  Ctrl+Shift+N: new layer  ·  Ctrl+E: merge down
Ctrl+T: free transform: frame the layer to move, scale or rotate it
Ctrl+0: fit on screen  ·  Ctrl+1: zoom to actual pixels  ·  + / −: zoom in / out
Space + drag: pan the canvas (or drag with the middle / right mouse button)
Shift + corner handle: stretch instead of scaling evenly (Move & Image)
Ctrl+S: save the design you're working on

My Designs

Your designs are saved in this browser on this device. Use ⤓ on a design to download a backup you can keep or move to another computer.

Shading Templates

Start from a premade fabric shading template. It drops soft folds and depth onto a new layer above your design: paint your colours on the layers underneath, then fine-tune its opacity or blend mode in the Layers panel.

Your uploads are saved in this browser and shown below.

Choose a theme

Pick the look of the studio. Your choice is saved on this device and remembered next time.

Import Full Template

This is for a shirt or pants picture you already finished somewhere else, such as a template you made in another app, or one you exported from here and want to carry on with.

What happens

It replaces this layer. Whatever is on it now gets rubbed out first.
Your other layers stay as they are. Only the one you have selected changes.
The picture is stretched to 585×559. If yours is a different size or shape, it will look squashed.
Changed your mind? Press Ctrl+Z straight after and it comes back.Tap the undo arrow at the top straight after and it comes back.

Mirror

Flip this layer to the other side of the body, so the right arm and leg swap with the left. Do you want to keep what's on this side too?

Want both sides to paint together while you draw instead? Turn on Symmetry above the canvas.
